newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA BULLION CLOSES DOWN ON WEAK GLOBAL TRENDS.
newsitem.headline: INDIA BULLION CLOSES DOWN ON WEAK GLOBAL TRENDS.

text.p: Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,465 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,480 rupees but up 10 rupees compared to the opening price of 4,455 rupees as renewed festival buying helped prices bounce back after early losses, dealer said.
Gold was down by 35 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday. Gold prices opened lower following a weak trend in the world market but fresh buying later dragged prices upward towards the close.
"Reports that customs officials have seized about 170/175 gold biscuits in Bombay also aided the recovery in the prices after an easy start," one broker said.
"The market is agog with the rumours that they were impostors and have actually looted the owners of the gold biscuits," he said.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.64 gramme) closed 200 rupees lower at 52,200 rupees per piece after losing 400 rupees on Wednesday.

Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees lower at 6,310 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,325 rupees. Silver opened lower at 6,300 rupees but eased pressure of arrivals helped it stage a modest recovery towards the close.
Silver was down by 105 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
